header:
Date: 2025-10-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Rosa Kim (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ruiz (Aurora CTO), Priya Singh (Aurora ML Eng), Erik Olsen (Aurora Platform Eng), Sana Ahmed (Aurora Security)
summary: Demo/walkthrough of Redwood Console 'Request Inspector' and tracing features. Focus on how to debug failing requests, analyze error distributions, correlate request logs with model variants and rollout policies, and extract per-request cost/latency. Customer asked about private deployment, KMS encryption, SOC2, and how console integrates with their pager/alerting. Agreed next steps: send security docs, perf/cost samples, and schedule POC scoping call.
topics: Request logs and raw payload visibility
Debugging flows: reproducing failures, replay, KV cache view
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can do intros quick. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Lucas is our SE, Rosa's on CSM.
[00:08] Daniel Ruiz: Hey all, Daniel here. We're about to kick off a small POC and wanted to understand how your console helps us debug production issues.
[00:14] Lucas Chen: Awesome, Daniel. Today we'll show the Request Inspector, tracing, error analysis, and how request logs tie back to models and rollout policies.
[00:22] Priya Singh: Great. A few specific asks: we want per-request latency and token cost, plus the ability to see model inputs at the time of the request (masked where needed), and quick ways to find regressions after model rollouts.
[00:36] Lucas Chen: Totally. We'll start with a quick deck then jump in the console. Quick note, some of the auto-transcription in our demo may read 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache' so if you see that, ignore it, that's the bot.
[00:48] Lucas Chen: (screenshare begins) Here is the Request Inspector list view. You can filter by model, route, status code, and request duration. I'm going to filter to the last 24 hours and show failed requests only.
[01:05] Priya Singh: Can you also group by model version? We frequently A/B roll and want to know if a model variant caused an uptick in errors.
[01:12] Lucas Chen: Yep, group by model.version is built-in. When we select group by, you see error rates per variant, and we show the top error signatures.
[01:22] [01:22] (brief hesitation)
[01:24] Lucas Chen: Here's an example where model-v2 shows a spike in tokenization errors — that might be due to tokenization mismatch after quantization.
[01:32] Daniel Ruiz: Tokenization errors? Could that be an artifact of the quantized runtime? We're planning to use quantized models in Dedicated.
[01:40] Lucas Chen: Sometimes quantization changes byte-level inputs, yes. The Console surfaces the raw input bytes and inferred tokenizer to help you debug. You can also replay the request against a pinned model variant with the same sequence length to debug locally.
[01:52] Priya Singh: Replay is critical. Can we replay with different cache states — like with or without KV cache warmed?
[01:58] Lucas Chen: Good question. We surface a 'replay' toggle. For cached-enabled routes we show the KV cache hit/miss histogram. You can replay with 'cold' or 'warm' cache snapshots if you previously recorded them — we store snapshots for the last N requests by default on Dedicated/Private. On Hosted it's more conservative for privacy.
[02:16] Sana Ahmed: About privacy: would replay payloads include PHI? We're healthcare and need to ensure PII is redacted and that logs don't persist PHI.
[02:24] Maya Patel: Short answer: we integrate with your KMS and can enable request redaction at ingestion. For Private deployments you control retention policies. We'll send the SOC2 + KMS/HSM docs after.
[02:36] Erik Olsen: How is that redaction enforced? Is it client-side or in the control plane?
[02:40] Rosa Kim: We have both options. There's client-side masking libraries and server-side ingestion rules. For Private you can also run an on-prem ingest proxy.
[02:48] Lucas Chen: Back to the Console: click into a single request — you'll see top pane with summary: model, route, latency breakdown (queueing, model inference, post-processing), and token counts. Then the timeline with timestamps and intermediate logs.
[03:05] [03:05] Lucas Chen: I'm hovering over a request with 1.2s model time; see that the KV cache had a 45% hit rate so we saved ~120ms.
[03:15] Priya Singh: Does the Console show per-request cost estimate? We need to plug that into our chargeback.
[03:20] Lucas Chen: Yes, under cost breakdown we show estimated token cost based on the model variant + quantization, plus infra estimate. It's a predictive estimate, and we can export CSV for a period.
[03:30] Daniel Ruiz: Can we map requests back to a user ID safely? We want to know if certain customers are generating noisy traffic, but we need role-based access control so only certain people can see raw inputs.
[03:40] Maya Patel: RBAC is available; you can restrict who sees full payload vs redacted summary. We support SAML SSO and SCIM for groups.
[03:48] Priya Singh: Show us error grouping — how do you dedupe similar stack traces?
[03:52] Lucas Chen: We use a fingerprinting approach: normalize variable tokens (like ids, timestamps) and hash the normalized trace. The Console shows a representative sample and counts. There is also a way to define custom fingerprint rules per route.
[04:04] [04:04] (crosstalk)
[04:06] Priya Singh: Nice. And alerting? We need to fire on error-rate upticks post-rollout.
[04:10] Lucas Chen: You can create alerts in the Console that trigger on a rate-change over baseline, absolute thresholds, or anomaly detection. Alerts can push to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhook.
[04:18] Erik Olsen: For Private, do alerts call our on-prem alert manager or call Redwood's control plane?
[04:23] Maya Patel: For VPC/private customers we offer a webhook integration that posts to your internal alert manager; no data leaves your VPC if you choose that option.
[04:31] Priya Singh: Re: replay, can we attach a debug container so the SE can reproduce with our exact env?
[04:35] Lucas Chen: We have a replay API that returns a sanitized payload and environment metadata; you can pull that into your local runtime. For sensitive data we provide a redacted replay artifact and an option for you to request a privileged view under audit.
[04:49] Daniel Ruiz: On rollout policies, can the Console correlate model rollout changes with downstream metric regressions?
[04:55] Lucas Chen: Yes — the rollout timeline shows deployed variants and config; when you click an incident it overlays the rollout timeline so you can visually correlate changes with latency/error spikes.
[05:06] Priya Singh: Ok can you show a real example?
[05:09] Lucas Chen: Sure, selecting a sample incident from last week — model-v3a rolled out at 02:06 UTC, and you see a latency bump + 7% error rate within 10 minutes. Here's the request fingerprint cluster where most failures came from.
[05:22] [05:22] (short pause)
[05:24] Lucas Chen: I'm going to open the raw trace — you see the tokenization step, then the runtime kernel selection log. Sometimes the transcription will call that 'kernel' as 'kernel sel' or 'carner' in the auto text, again apologies for that.
[05:36] Priya Singh: (laughs) no worries. For the POC we want to validate two things: 1) the tracing fidelity when we run on Dedicated GPU pool, and 2) the cost delta sticking to quantized vs fp16.
[05:48] Maya Patel: We can run a short benchmark and share a CSV. Lucas will prepare a template you can run against a small sample of production traffic or synthetic traces.
[05:56] Sana Ahmed: A few security questions: data residency, retention windows, how long request logs live by default, and whether we can turn off all request persistence in hosted mode.
[06:06] Maya Patel: Default retention in Hosted is 30 days for full payloads, 90 for metrics; but for healthcare customers we recommend Private to meet residency and retention needs. You can configure retention to zero for payloads on ingest. We'll include options in the security doc.
[06:20] Erik Olsen: If we go Dedicated, do we still get the Console UI hosted by Redwood or is there a private Console?
[06:26] Lucas Chen: Dedicated customers get an isolated tenant in our control plane and can optionally have the Console served through a private endpoint. Private on-prem customers can run a control plane behind their VPC.
[06:36] Daniel Ruiz: Good. Any limitations on a replay for very long contexts or extremely large KV caches?
[06:42] Lucas Chen: For very long contexts we sample the trace and surface a trimmed version, with links to the archived blob if retention allows. For large KV caches we show a summarized diff and top keys; full dumps are possible on Dedicated/Private if you opt in.
[06:56] Priya Singh: Let's talk about observability integrations — we use Datadog and Prometheus.
[07:00] Lucas Chen: We push metrics to Datadog and Prometheus out-of-the-box and have tracing correlations with OpenTelemetry. We can attach trace_ids to your APM traces so you can jump from Datadog to the Request Inspector.
[07:10] Rosa Kim: And we provide webhooks for new incidents so you can create tickets in Jira automatically.
[07:16] Daniel Ruiz: OK, timecheck we have about 10 minutes left. Can you summarize the POC proposal?
[07:22] Maya Patel: Sure — proposed POC: 4-week pilot on Dedicated pool with sample traffic, enable request-level tracing and redaction, run two short benchmarks (fp16 vs quantized), and validate alerting to your PagerDuty. Lucas will own benchmarks, I will own the security docs and POC contract, and Erik will share infra constraints.
[07:40] Priya Singh: Sounds good. For the contract we need an NDA addendum re: PHI.
[07:44] Maya Patel: Noted — we'll include that in the docs.
[07:48] [07:48] (screen stops sharing)
[07:50] Daniel Ruiz: Quick question about pricing — is there a per-request debug fee?
[07:54] Maya Patel: No separate debug fee; usage-based pricing applies. There may be additional fees for high-retention logs or large KV snapshot exports in Dedicated. We'll include explicit numbers in the pricing sheet.
[08:06] Erik Olsen: Great. Any other questions?
[08:08] (silence)
[08:10] Priya Singh: Nope, that's it from me.
[08:12] Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll send the SOC2 and KMS notes and Lucas will send the benchmark template. Proposed follow-up: Oct 9th for scoping with infra.
[08:22] Daniel Ruiz: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[08:26] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[08:28] [END]
